findings.title: The tooling-vs-product split is a classification choice, and "roughly half" is defensible at 30 days
findings.claim: Over the last 30 days, commits Jason authored split 512 product / 192 tooling / 7 exploration on the finder's repo classification, which is 27.0% tooling. That verdict is not robust: reclassifying brok-stacks (116 human commits in 30d) and unifi (21) as household infrastructure rather than product puts it at 329/711 = 46.3%, so the brief's "roughly half" is a defensible reading of the same 30 days. The tooling share does climb inside the window, from roughly 20% (Aug 06-12) to 36-44% (since Aug 27), but not to half once ambient's tooling share is measured rather than assumed.
findings.evidence: GitHub API pull across 57 repos under jasonm4130 + jasonm4130-labs, REVIEW/out/E3-shipping/commits30.tsv: 512/192/7 = 27.0%; brok-stacks+unifi reclassified = 329/711 = 46.3%. Ambient measured directly: 9 of 86 non-merge commits since 2026-08-01 touch loop/ (verified in /Users/jasonmatthew/Work/Git/ambient), and 791 of 50,072 lines changed, against the 31.3% the finder assumed.
findings.action: Do not quote a single tooling-share number without saying which repos count as product. Publish the classification with the number, or quote the two bounds (27% and 46%).

findings.title: Coach's commit count is 68% agent-written, so raw commit counts overstate its effort about 3x
findings.claim: Coach shows 460 non-merge commits in August, 311 by the `claude` identity (67.6%) and 149 by Jason; in September it is claude 17 / Jason 0. Of the 502 agent-authored commits since April, 450 are Coach (89.6%). Any effort or throughput accounting built on the brief's "Coach 406 commits" reads a product's own logging behaviour as engineering labour.

findings.title: The general crowding-out hypothesis fails: July was peak tooling and peak product at once
findings.claim: July was both the peak tooling month (253 tooling commits, 17.6% share) and the peak product month (1,161 product commits, 37.5/day). Tooling and product rose together, so the general form of "tooling costs product" does not survive. The [ship]-win count corroborates only weakly: the vault logging automation landed 2026-06-21 and its standing-approval rule 2026-07-05, and wins/day step at exactly those boundaries (0.9 to 1.8 to 3.4 to 5.7), so the Jun-to-Jul win jump is partly an instrumentation change.
findings.evidence: Class table by month, human-authored non-merge: 04 433p/32t, 05 735p/91t, 06 643p/46t, 07 1161p/253t, 08 635p/161t, 09(1-5) 51p/44t (verifier reproduced July within 2 commits). Vault '## 🏆 Wins' [ship] lines: Jun 36, Jul 166, Aug 91, Sep 1-5 14, reproduced to the unit. chezmoi f8a2086 (2026-06-21) daily-notes automation; c831ae8 (2026-07-05) standing-approved vault logging.
findings.action: Drop the general crowding-out claim. Treat any vault-derived output measure as instrumented from 2026-06-21 and again from 2026-07-05, and do not compare across those dates.

findings.title: The August output drop is the day job, and tooling took only a fifth of the cut
findings.claim: The weekday 09:00-17:00 share of commits collapsed from 54.0% (W32) through 26.6% (W33) to 0.0%, 0.0% and 3.8% (W34-36). The day job started 2026-08-17, written verbatim in the vault daily note. The remaining hours were not split proportionally: tooling fell 7.7 to 6.1 commits/day (-21%) while product fell 31 to 5.2/day (-83%), and in the last three days tooling ran at 13.1 commits/day, its highest rate in the whole 30-day window.
findings.evidence: Weekday-daytime share recomputed independently over ten local clones with author dates and --author='Jason': W30 20.2%, W31 30.9%, W32 54.0%, W33 26.6%, W34 0.0%, W35 0.0%, W36 3.8%. /Users/jasonmatthew/Documents/Main/Daily/2026-08-17 - Daily.md: "- [x] First day at the new job ✅ 2026-08-17" (I re-read this line). Ship-wins/day 4.5 (Aug 1-16) to 1.3 (Aug 17-31). The absolute weekly totals did not reproduce between finder and verifier and should not be quoted.
findings.action: Set an explicit weekly tooling budget as a fraction of the hours that now exist (e.g. one evening in five) and check it against the same commit split weekly. The scarce resource changed in mid-August and the allocation did not.

findings.title: Nightshift has never run unattended: every landing was a supervised daylight debug run
findings.claim: All 30 loop starts across five journals happened on 2026-09-05 between 05:57 and 16:22; the launchd job is scheduled for 02:00 and its log holds one manual 06:26 invocation that landed nothing. Twelve starts were dry runs. Nine PRs landed at $36.87 of metered API price, $4.10 per landed PR, which is notional because Jason is on a Max plan: the payback unit is plan capacity and wall clock, not money. The unattended-overnight thesis has not been tested once.
findings.evidence: Five journals under ~/.local/state/nightshift/ (ambient, ambient-hardening, ambient-live-asr, ambient-session-tools, claude-skills); ~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.nightshift.ambient.plist StartCalendarInterval Hour=2 Minute=0; ~/.local/state/nightshift/ambient/launchd.log has exactly one entry (06:26, max 0, nothing landed). Cost $36.87 over 37 agent calls across all five journals ($32.90 across the two the finder read).
findings.action: Wait for three consecutive 02:00 runs, then report PRs landed in the 02:00-07:00 window per night, blocked-task rate, and wall-clock hours consumed. Nothing before that is evidence about the loop. Report capacity, not dollars.

findings.title: Seven of nine Nightshift landings are internal quality work; two are user-visible
findings.claim: Seven of the nine landed PRs are internal quality infrastructure: a WER scorer, a LibriSpeech fixture, a scoring harness, a quality script, log_mel tests and two doc corrections. Two are user-visible: #46 adds `show --json` to the CLI (src/main.rs, src/session.rs, docs/using/commands.md) and #47 fixes NaN-safe argmax across src/asr.rs, src/diarize.rs, src/features.rs and src/vad.rs. The original "nothing user-visible" claim was true of the first seven PRs and false of the run an hour later.
findings.evidence: `gh pr list -R jasonm4130-labs/ambient --state merged`, head branches land/*: #19 43L, #22 22L, #24 52L, #32 228L, #33 244L, #42 212L, #43 177L, plus #46 and #47 merged 2026-09-05T06:38-06:39Z; claude-skills #102 105L. Note the finder's stated proof that #43 was hand-merged (mergedBy jasonm4130) does not hold: the loop merges with Jason's token, so mergedBy is jasonm4130 on all nine. The real evidence is the absence of a "landed as PR #43" journal line.
findings.action: Write into the plan template which of the two jobs the loop has. If it is meant to ship product, a plan whose tasks are all test scaffolding is the wrong plan. Never infer loop authorship from mergedBy.

findings.title: 61% of the July plugin build is gone
findings.claim: The marketplace peaked at 18 plugins on 2026-07-31 and holds 9 today. Eight were retired outright (adversarial-agents, claude-design, codebase-design, deep-dive, frontend-design, subagent-driven-development, superpowers-core, visual-plan) and three guards were folded into `gates`, so 11 of the 18 (61%) no longer exist as plugins. findings.title: Four of six model-invocable owned plugins were used; the measurable gap is session-retro at zero
findings.claim: Of the nine enabled owned plugins, three (gates, ship-gate, nightshift) expose no model-invocable skill, so their zero is structural. Of the six that do, four were invoked in the local 15-day window: codex-plan-review 7, writing-artifacts 3, domain-modeling 1, adr 1, which is 12 of 38 total invocations. Two were not: session-retro, and handoff, whose auto-fire was deliberately disabled on 2026-08-08 because compaction now continues the session. findings.title: The pack reproduced Jason's known model failure mode: a confident negative with no positive check
findings.claim: The finder filed the day-job start date as one of three things it could not establish, writing that the vault notes "never name a first day", and inferred 2026-08-17 from commit timing instead. The date is written verbatim in the vault. This is the same failure the standing CLAUDE.md rule names ("a confident negative needs a positive proof") and that the pack lists as unchanged across periods, occurring inside the review itself, in an agent that had the file on disk.
findings.evidence: Finder's `gaps` field: "the notes themselves never name a first day, so the confound's timing is inferred, not read." I grepped the file: /Users/jasonmatthew/Documents/Main/Daily/2026-08-17 - Daily.md contains "- [x] First day at the new job ✅ 2026-08-17". One `grep -ril "first day"` over the July-August dailies finds it.
findings.action: Make the positive-check demand executable rather than advisory: require any agent filing an "unresolvable gap" to name and run the command that would find it. The prose rule alone did not fire here.
